title: Evaluation of the effect of adrenalized lidocaine with or without bicarbonate on early postoperative recovery in ambulatory hand and foot surgery with WALANT
official: Evaluation of the effect of adrenalized lidocaine with or without bicarbonate on early postoperative recovery in ambulatory hand and foot surgery with WALANT: A Single-centre prospective randomised double-blind non-inferiority study.
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effect of two WALANT-type local anaesthetic protocols (with or without the addition of bicarbonate) on early postoperative recovery in ambulatory hand and foot surgery under WALANT.

interventions.name: BICARBONATE DE SODIUM 8,4% B. BRAUN, solution pour perfusion
CHLORURE DE SODIUM FRESENIUS 0,9 %, solution pour perfusion
XYLOCAINE 10 mg/ml ADRENALINE 0,005 mg/ml, solution injectable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient eligible for outpatient surgery under WALANT for : Hand surgery such as carpal tunnel, stub finger, Dupuytren's disease; Foot surgery (hallux valgus or rigidus).
2. Patient has given free and informed consent.
3. Patient who has signed the consent form.
4. Patient affiliated to or benefiting from a health insurance.
5. Adult patient (≥18 years).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Ischaemic vascular disorders such as severe Raynaud's disease, Buerger's disease and diabetic microangiopathy.
2. Severe arterial hypertension.
3. Obstructive cardiomyopathy.
4. Hyperthyroidism
5. Hypovolaemia
6. Patient participating in an interventional RIPH defined in category 1
7. Patient in an exclusion period determined by another study
8. Patient under court protection, guardianship or curatorship
9. Patient unable to give consent
10. Patients for whom it is impossible to provide informed information
11. Pregnant, parturient or breast-feeding patients
12. Scleroderma.
13. Known allergy to lidocaine and possibility of cross-allergy with other amide-linked local anaesthetics.
14. Severe hepatic impairment
15. Acute porphyria
16. Intravascular anaesthesia
17. Local infiltration anaesthesia in the extremities
18. Coronary insufficiency
19. Ventricular rhythm disorders
